issue_description: Centrifugal pump makes a loud grinding noise and vibrates heavily during operation.
root_cause: Worn or failed bearings, often caused by lack of lubrication or contamination.
recommended_fix: Shut down the pump, replace the bearings, flush old grease and re-lubricate to manufacturer spec. Check shaft alignment before restart.

issue_description: Pump is leaking oil around the shaft seal and there is an oil puddle under the housing.
root_cause: Degraded mechanical shaft seal or an over-filled oil reservoir.
recommended_fix: Isolate and drain the pump, replace the mechanical seal, verify the oil level is within the sight-glass marks, then check for leaks under load.

issue_description: Pump runs but flow rate and discharge pressure are lower than normal.
root_cause: Partially clogged suction strainer or impeller wear reducing hydraulic efficiency.
recommended_fix: Clean the suction strainer, inspect the impeller for wear or debris, and replace it if clearance exceeds tolerance.

issue_description: Pump makes a crackling or gravel-like rattling sound and pressure fluctuates.
root_cause: Cavitation caused by insufficient suction head, a blocked inlet line or an air leak on the suction side.
recommended_fix: Check the inlet valve is fully open, clear suction blockages, tighten suction flanges, and confirm the fluid level meets the required NPSH.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute (pumps.org) - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: Pump casing is warm and there is a slow drip from the packing gland.
root_cause: Packing gland is slightly loose or the packing has reached end of life.
recommended_fix: Adjust gland follower nuts evenly to restore a slight drip, or repack the gland at the next planned maintenance window.

issue_description: Electric motor is overheating and there is a burning smell near the windings.
root_cause: Overloaded motor, blocked cooling airflow or insulation breakdown in the windings.
recommended_fix: Stop the motor immediately, let it cool, clear the cooling fins and fan cover, measure winding insulation resistance, and rewind or replace if insulation is degraded.

issue_description: Motor hums but will not start turning, and the breaker sometimes trips.
root_cause: Failed start capacitor, single-phasing from a lost supply phase, or a seized rotor.
recommended_fix: Isolate power, check all three phases at the terminals, test the start capacitor, and rotate the shaft by hand to rule out a mechanical seizure.

issue_description: Motor has a high-pitched squealing noise that gets louder as it speeds up.
root_cause: Dry or worn motor bearings, or a loose drive belt slipping on the pulley.
recommended_fix: Lubricate or replace the bearings and inspect the drive belt tension and pulley alignment.

issue_description: Motor vibrates excessively and the mounting bolts keep loosening.
root_cause: Shaft misalignment, unbalanced rotor or loose foundation.
recommended_fix: Perform laser alignment on the coupling, balance the rotor if needed, and re-torque the baseplate and mounting bolts with thread locker.

issue_description: Motor runs slightly warmer than before but performance is normal.
root_cause: Dust buildup on the motor casing reducing heat dissipation.
recommended_fix: Clean the motor casing and cooling fins during the next scheduled maintenance and log temperature readings.

issue_description: Printer has a paper jam and the paper is crumpled inside the feed path.
root_cause: Worn pickup rollers or incorrect paper type and humidity-damaged paper.
recommended_fix: Power off, remove all jammed paper gently, clean or replace the pickup rollers, and reload fresh paper of the correct weight.

issue_description: Printed pages have black streaks and smudges down the page.
root_cause: Dirty or damaged drum, or leaking toner cartridge.
recommended_fix: Replace the toner cartridge, clean the drum and corona wire, and print a few test pages to clear residual toner.

issue_description: Printer shows a fuser error code and pages come out with toner that smears off.
root_cause: Failing fuser assembly that no longer reaches the correct temperature.
recommended_fix: Power down and let the fuser cool, then replace the fuser unit. Do not keep printing, as unfused toner contaminates the machine.

issue_description: Printer is not detected by the network and shows as offline for all users.
root_cause: IP address conflict, lost network configuration or a faulty network card.
recommended_fix: Print a configuration page, assign a static IP, restart the print spooler on the server, and replace the network interface if it still fails.

issue_description: Printer emits smoke and a strong burning smell from the rear panel.
root_cause: Electrical fault in the power supply unit or overheated fuser components.
recommended_fix: Unplug the printer immediately, do not power it on again, and arrange a qualified technician to inspect and replace the power supply.

issue_description: Air conditioner is running but blowing warm air and not cooling the room.
root_cause: Low refrigerant charge from a leak, or a failed compressor.
recommended_fix: Check refrigerant pressures, locate and repair any leak, recharge to specification, and test compressor amp draw.
source_name: Carrier - Why is my AC blowing hot air?

issue_description: HVAC unit makes a loud banging or rattling noise from the blower section.
root_cause: Loose or unbalanced blower wheel, or a failing blower motor bearing.
recommended_fix: Turn off the unit, inspect and tighten the blower wheel set screw, clean the wheel, and replace the blower motor if the bearing is worn.

issue_description: Water is dripping from the indoor air handler and pooling on the floor.
root_cause: Clogged condensate drain line or a frozen evaporator coil that has melted.
recommended_fix: Flush the condensate drain with a wet vacuum and cleaning solution, replace the air filter, and check for low airflow causing coil icing.
source_name: Lennox - Why is your air conditioner leaking water?

issue_description: Outdoor condenser unit will not start and the fan is not spinning.
root_cause: Failed run capacitor or contactor, or a tripped high-pressure switch.
recommended_fix: Disconnect power, test and replace the capacitor or contactor, and verify the high-pressure switch has not locked out.

issue_description: Strong refrigerant or chemical smell and oily residue near the compressor of the cooling unit.
root_cause: Refrigerant leak at a fitting or coil joint, creating a safety and environmental hazard.
recommended_fix: Shut the unit down, ventilate the area, have a certified technician locate and repair the leak and recover and recharge refrigerant per regulation.

issue_description: Conveyor belt is drifting to one side and rubbing against the frame.
root_cause: Belt tracking misalignment from uneven tension or a misaligned roller.
recommended_fix: Stop the conveyor, adjust the take-up tensioners evenly, realign the head and tail pulleys, and re-run the belt empty to confirm tracking.

issue_description: Conveyor belt is slipping and the drive pulley spins without moving the belt.
root_cause: Insufficient belt tension or worn lagging on the drive pulley.
recommended_fix: Increase belt tension via the take-up, inspect and replace worn pulley lagging, and clear any material buildup.

issue_description: Conveyor belt has a visible tear and frayed edge along its length.
root_cause: Sharp material impact, snagging on the frame, or edge wear from misalignment.
recommended_fix: Stop the conveyor and apply lockout. Repair with a vulcanized splice or mechanical fastener for small tears, or replace the belt section for large damage.

issue_description: Conveyor idler rollers squeak and a few rollers no longer turn.
root_cause: Seized idler bearings from dust ingress and lack of lubrication.
recommended_fix: Replace the seized idlers, grease the remaining ones on schedule, and install dust shields where material spills.

issue_description: Diesel generator fails to start and the engine only cranks slowly.
root_cause: Weak or discharged starting battery, or corroded battery terminals.
recommended_fix: Test and charge the battery, clean and tighten the terminals, and replace the battery if it fails a load test.

issue_description: Generator produces black smoke from the exhaust and loses power under load.
root_cause: Clogged air filter, dirty fuel injectors, or the engine being overloaded.
recommended_fix: Replace the air filter, service or clean the fuel injectors, and verify the connected load is within the rated capacity.

issue_description: Generator shut down automatically with a low oil pressure alarm and oil is leaking from the engine.
root_cause: Oil leak from a gasket or filter seal leading to dangerously low oil level.
recommended_fix: Do not restart. Locate and repair the leak, refill with the correct oil grade, replace the oil filter, and verify oil pressure at idle before returning to service.
source_name: Generac Support - Low oil pressure, error code 1300

issue_description: Generator output voltage is unstable and the lights flicker when the generator is running.
root_cause: Faulty automatic voltage regulator (AVR) or governor hunting due to dirty fuel.
recommended_fix: Test and replace the AVR if its output is erratic, replace the fuel filter, and check governor linkage for smooth movement.

issue_description: Pump runs but delivers little or no liquid and sounds like it is running dry.
root_cause: Air in the pump or suction line because it was never primed, or the liquid level is too low or the intake is not submerged enough, letting air vortices in.
recommended_fix: 1) Stop the pump. 2) Make sure the liquid floods the pump to prime it before every start. 3) Check the liquid level over the intake and raise it if needed. 4) Restart and watch pressure.
safety_note: Do not run a pump dry: the seal and bearings can be destroyed within minutes.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute (pumps.org) - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: New three-phase pump starts but gives low pressure and very little flow, and sounds loud.
root_cause: The motor is turning the wrong way, because two electrical leads are in the wrong order.
recommended_fix: 1) Isolate the motor. 2) Have an electrician swap any two of the three leads. 3) Check the rotation arrow before running again.
safety_note: Electrical work only by a qualified electrician; check rotation before running the pump loaded.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute (pumps.org) - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: Pump pressure is lower than the performance curve although nothing leaks outside.
root_cause: Air being pulled in at the suction side through poorly tightened bolts or a cut gasket (negative inlet pressure leaks do not show as an outward leak).
recommended_fix: 1) Check the suction-side flange bolts and gaskets. 2) Replace a cut gasket. 3) Re-test pressure.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute (pumps.org) - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: Pump gives less pressure after the liquid was changed or got colder.
root_cause: The new liquid has a different viscosity or density from the one the pump curve is based on.
recommended_fix: 1) Compare the actual fluid properties with the curve. 2) Warm the liquid if cold thickens it. 3) Re-size the pump if the new fluid is permanent.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute (pumps.org) - Why pump pressure is lower than expected

issue_description: Pump motor draws more current than expected and runs hot.
root_cause: The pump runs at higher flow or head than designed, the liquid is denser or more viscous, or internal wear and friction (seals, packing, bearings) have increased losses.
recommended_fix: 1) Compare actual flow and head with the pump curve. 2) Check the liquid properties. 3) Look for tight packing, worn seals or bearings. 4) Check alignment and pipe strain.
source_name: Hydraulic Institute (pumps.org) - Why pump power is higher than expected

issue_description: Heating circulator pump is noisy, with gurgling or whooshing in the pipes.
root_cause: Air in the pump, or inlet pressure that is too low.
recommended_fix: 1) Put the pump on its highest speed for about 30 minutes to vent it, then set it back. 2) If it persists, call a professional installer to correct the system pressure.
source_name: Grundfos Support - Why is the circulator pump making noise?

issue_description: Motor is overloaded: it trips and the windings are evenly darkened with age.
root_cause: The motor is asked to deliver more power than it was sized for.
recommended_fix: 1) Measure the current against the nameplate. 2) Reduce the load or fit a larger motor.
source_name: Electrical Academia - Electric motor failure causes, symptoms and remedies

issue_description: Three-phase motor runs hot and loses power even though the load is normal.
root_cause: Voltage unbalance between the phases, so one winding overheats.
recommended_fix: 1) Measure the voltage on all three phases at the motor. 2) Look for heavy single-phase loads on one line. 3) Ask the power company or an electrician to balance the supply, or derate the motor.
safety_note: Electrical measurement and repairs: qualified electrician only.
source_name: Electrical Academia - Electric motor failure causes, symptoms and remedies

issue_description: Motor hums and burns out one coil, with a burnt smell, after a fuse blew.
root_cause: Single-phasing: one phase was lost from a blown fuse, switching fault or lightning.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the fuse with the correct rating. 2) Fit a phase-loss monitor. 3) Have the motor checked or rewound.
safety_note: Isolate the supply before inspecting the motor.
source_name: Electrical Academia - Electric motor failure causes, symptoms and remedies

issue_description: Motor in an enclosed cabinet or a dusty place keeps overheating.
root_cause: Airflow is blocked by dust, dirt or oil, or the enclosure recirculates hot air.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the motor and fan guard. 2) Add ventilation openings to the enclosure. 3) Stop oil collecting on the motor.
source_name: Electrical Academia - Electric motor failure causes, symptoms and remedies

issue_description: Belt-driven motor squeals and its bearings get hot.
root_cause: The belt is too tight or too loose, which overloads the bearing or lets the belt slip.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the belt deflection with a straight-edge or tension tester. 2) Re-tension to the maker's value.
safety_note: Stop and lock out before touching belts and pulleys.
source_name: Electrical Academia - Electric motor failure causes, symptoms and remedies

issue_description: Motor and driven machine vibrate and the bearings keep failing.
root_cause: The motor shaft and the load shaft are misaligned.
recommended_fix: 1) Realign with shims. 2) Use a flexible coupling if exact alignment is not possible. 3) Replace damaged bearings.
safety_note: Lock out before working on the coupling.
source_name: Electrical Academia - Electric motor failure causes, symptoms and remedies

issue_description: Motor that sits idle for long periods is rusty and trips on insulation resistance.
root_cause: Moist air drawn in during cooling cycles and long shutdowns damages the insulation.
recommended_fix: 1) Dry the windings. 2) Fit space heaters in the motor. 3) Run idle motors on a maintenance schedule.
source_name: Electrical Academia - Electric motor failure causes, symptoms and remedies

issue_description: Paper jams inside the fuser area and the sheet is wrapped around the fuser roller.
root_cause: Paper outside the printer's specification, mixed paper types in one tray, an overfull stack or tray guides in the wrong position.
recommended_fix: 1) Open the access door and pull the jammed sheet out gently with both hands. 2) Fan the paper and load it below the max line. 3) Set the guides and the paper type in the menu correctly. 4) Print a test page.
safety_note: The fuser is hot: let it cool before touching, and never use sharp tools to remove paper.
source_name: Lexmark Support - Paper jams in the fuser (C792)

issue_description: Paper is stuck behind the rear door where the fuser sits.
root_cause: A sheet stopped in the fuser during printing.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch off and wait at least 40 minutes for the fuser to cool. 2) Open the rear door, lift the fuser levers and paper guide. 3) Remove all paper. 4) Close everything and restart.
safety_note: The fuser unit can be very hot: wait for it to cool.
source_name: Xerox Support - Clear a paper jam from the fuser area (VersaLink B405)

issue_description: Colour laser prints show lines and spots down every page.
root_cause: Dirt in the paper path, soiled printhead lenses or transfer belt, old or damp paper or paper that does not meet specifications.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the printhead lenses with the built-in tool. 2) Reseat the drum cartridges and waste toner container. 3) Print the repeating-defects page to find the part. 4) Replace the drum cartridge or fuser if the defect remains.
safety_note: The belt cleaner blade is very sharp and the fuser is hot: handle carefully.
source_name: Xerox Support - Streaks, lines or spots on copies and prints

issue_description: Printouts come out pale or faded across the whole page.
root_cause: Toner running low, a worn drum or a wrong paper type setting.
recommended_fix: 1) Shake or replace the toner cartridge. 2) Check the toner-saver setting. 3) Set the correct paper type.

issue_description: Printer prints blank pages.
root_cause: An empty cartridge, a missing seal tape on a new cartridge, or a failed transfer or drum unit.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the cartridge has toner and the seal tape was removed. 2) Reseat the cartridge. 3) Try another cartridge or call service.

issue_description: Printer says paper jam but nothing is stuck.
root_cause: A dirty paper sensor, torn paper scrap left inside, or a stuck flag.
recommended_fix: 1) Open all doors and look for small scraps. 2) Clean the paper sensors gently. 3) Power cycle the printer.

issue_description: Air conditioner never starts or cools even though it is switched on.
root_cause: The thermostat is set wrongly (not on cool, fan on instead of auto), or its batteries are flat.
recommended_fix: 1) Set the thermostat to Cool and fan to Auto. 2) Replace the batteries. 3) Set the target a few degrees below room temperature.
source_name: Carrier - Why is my AC blowing hot air?

issue_description: Outdoor AC unit is silent and the breaker has tripped.
root_cause: A tripped breaker or blown fuse from an electrical fault.
recommended_fix: 1) Reset the breaker once. 2) If it trips again at once, leave it off and call a professional.
safety_note: A breaker that re-trips immediately means an overload or electrical hazard.
source_name: Lennox - Outside AC unit not turning on

issue_description: AC outdoor unit buzzes or hums but the fan and compressor do not start.
root_cause: A failed capacitor in the outdoor unit: the buzzing or humming is the usual sign that it can no longer start the fan and compressor.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch off the power. 2) Have a professional HVAC technician test and replace the capacitor.
safety_note: Capacitors hold a charge: only a qualified technician should replace them.
source_name: Lennox - Outside AC unit not turning on

issue_description: Ice has formed on the indoor coil and the AC airflow is poor.
root_cause: A frozen coil from low airflow, usually a dirty filter, or low refrigerant.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch the system off and let the coil thaw completely. 2) Replace the air filter. 3) If it freezes again, have the refrigerant checked.
source_name: Lennox - Outside AC unit not turning on

issue_description: AC shuts down by itself and water collects near the indoor unit.
root_cause: A tripped float switch caused by a clogged condensate drain line.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean and clear the condensate drain line. 2) Replace the float switch if it is faulty.
source_name: Lennox - Outside AC unit not turning on

issue_description: Weak airflow from the vents and the house does not cool well.
root_cause: A clogged air filter or a blocked outdoor coil or indoor vents.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the filter (every one to three months). 2) Clear plants and debris from around the outdoor unit. 3) Clean the evaporator coil gently.
source_name: Carrier - Why is my AC blowing hot air?

issue_description: Belt splice is coming apart or fasteners are worn and rip the belt.
root_cause: An unskived splice, fasteners that interfere with the belt cleaners, or fasteners too big for the smallest pulley.
recommended_fix: 1) Skive the belt properly before splicing. 2) Use low-profile fasteners with coined edges. 3) Check pulley diameters against the fastener maker's limits.
source_name: Flexco - Top 10 belt conveyor quick fixes

issue_description: Material spills at the loading point and the belt gets damaged there.
root_cause: Weak skirting or not enough impact protection at the load zone.
recommended_fix: 1) Fit easy-service skirting. 2) Add impact protection suited to the weight of the lumps.
source_name: Flexco - Top 10 belt conveyor quick fixes

issue_description: Belt has cuts and gouges along its edge or surface.
root_cause: Rollers have seized and developed sharp flat spots that cut the belt.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace seized steel rollers with flat spots at once. 2) Replace composite rollers when practical. 3) Include idler turning checks in routine inspection.
safety_note: Lock out the conveyor before working near rollers.
source_name: Flexco - Top 10 belt conveyor quick fixes

issue_description: Belt edges lift and the belt will not lie flat, so it tracks badly (cupped belt).
root_cause: The belt is wider than the trough capacity or is over-tensioned.
recommended_fix: 1) Check tension and trough alignment. 2) Check how the belt settles empty. 3) Fix support so the belt sits on the carrying idlers.
source_name: Martin Engineering - 13 types of conveyor belt damage

issue_description: Belt top cover shows narrow surface cracks.
root_cause: The belt is bent over pulleys smaller than it was designed for.
recommended_fix: 1) Match the belt to the pulley size. 2) Replace the belt or pulleys if the bend radius is wrong.
source_name: Martin Engineering - 13 types of conveyor belt damage

issue_description: Belt plies are separating and the edges swell in a wet plant.
root_cause: Moisture soaking into the carcass of a cut-edge belt.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch to a moisture-resistant moulded-edge belt. 2) Keep the belt as dry as practical.
source_name: Martin Engineering - 13 types of conveyor belt damage

issue_description: Portable generator will not start or runs roughly.
root_cause: Fuel valve off, an empty tank, old fuel, water in fuel, a dirty air filter, a disconnected spark plug lead or bad spark plug, over-choking, low oil or a clogged carburettor.
recommended_fix: 1) Turn the fuel valve on and refill with fresh fuel. 2) Clean or replace the air filter. 3) Reconnect or replace the spark plug. 4) Fill the oil to the mark. 5) Clean the carburettor.
safety_note: Run generators outdoors only: exhaust contains deadly carbon monoxide.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Generator runs but there is no AC output at the sockets.
root_cause: The circuit breaker is open, a poor cord connection, a defective connected device, a tripped GFCI socket or an internal fault.
recommended_fix: 1) Reset the breaker. 2) Check the cord. 3) Test with another device. 4) Press the GFCI reset. 5) Call an authorised dealer for internal faults.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Generator engine slows or bogs down when the load is connected.
root_cause: A short circuit in the load, an overloaded generator, engine speed too low, a clogged carburettor or spark arrestor, or stale fuel.
recommended_fix: 1) Disconnect the faulty device. 2) Reduce the load. 3) Clean the carburettor and spark arrestor. 4) Replace old fuel.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Generator shuts down on its own while running.
root_cause: Out of fuel, low oil, or its carbon monoxide protection has tripped.
recommended_fix: 1) Refill fuel and oil. 2) If the CO warning light is on, move the generator to open air away from windows and doors.
safety_note: A CO alert means dangerous exhaust gas: relocate the generator outdoors, far from openings.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Generator engine surges up and down or lacks power.
root_cause: The choke was opened too soon, a carburettor imbalance, an overload or a dirty air filter.
recommended_fix: 1) Set the choke to the halfway position while warming up. 2) Reduce the load. 3) Clean or replace the air filter. 4) Call a service dealer for carburettor balance.
source_name: Generac Support - Portable generator troubleshooting quick reference guide

issue_description: Compressor will not start at all when the start button is pressed.
root_cause: No incoming power, an open emergency stop or door interlock, a tripped motor overload relay, or (on piston machines) an unloader that is not working.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the supply voltage and the isolator. 2) Check the emergency stop and cabinet door interlocks. 3) Read the controller fault history. 4) Reset a tripped overload only after finding why it tripped. 5) On a piston compressor confirm the unloader works.
safety_note: Checking supply voltage means working in a live panel: only a qualified electrician should do it, with proper PPE.
source_name: Fabrico - Air compressor troubleshooting

issue_description: Compressor runs normally but tank or line pressure never rises, or stays too low.
root_cause: Screw machines: blocked intake filter, sticking inlet valve, stuck minimum-pressure valve, failed separator element or a slipping belt. Piston machines: broken valves, leaking head gasket or worn rings.
recommended_fix: 1) Shut the compressor off from the plant to tell a supply problem from a demand problem. 2) Check, in order, intake filter, inlet valve, minimum-pressure valve and separator. 3) Check belt tension. 4) On a piston unit inspect valves and head gasket.
safety_note: Lock out power and vent trapped pressure from every section before opening it.
source_name: Fabrico - Air compressor troubleshooting

issue_description: A lot of hissing in the plant air lines and the compressor never stops running.
root_cause: Leaks at pipe joints, couplings and hose ends quietly eat compressor capacity.
recommended_fix: 1) Spray soapy water on suspect joints or scan with an ultrasonic leak detector. 2) Run an overnight pressure-decay test to measure the loss. 3) Tag each leak, repair it and retest on a regular schedule.
source_name: Fabrico - Air compressor troubleshooting

issue_description: Compressor shuts down on a high temperature trip or runs very hot.
root_cause: Low or wrong oil, clogged cooler cores, a failed cooling fan, a stuck thermostatic valve, or hot exhaust air recirculating in a badly ventilated compressor room.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the oil level and oil type. 2) Clean the cooler cores. 3) Check the cooling fans and motors. 4) Test the thermostatic valve. 5) Improve ventilation or ducting of the room.
safety_note: Discharge lines and coolers stay burn-hot long after shutdown.
source_name: Fabrico - Air compressor troubleshooting

issue_description: Water keeps coming out of the air lines and tools.
root_cause: Automatic drains have failed, the dryer is undersized or struggling in hot humid weather, or there is no aftercooler.
recommended_fix: 1) Test every automatic drain by hand. 2) Compare the dryer dew point with its rating. 3) Size the dryer for the hottest season rather than the yearly average. 4) Confirm the aftercooler works.
source_name: Fabrico - Air compressor troubleshooting

issue_description: Oil is showing up in the compressed air downstream, with an oily smell or film.
root_cause: An old or blinded separator element, an over-filled sump, a blocked scavenge line, or foaming from the wrong or degraded oil.
recommended_fix: 1) Change the separator element by running hours, not by how it looks. 2) Correct the oil level. 3) Clear the scavenge line. 4) Use the specified oil and replace it when degraded.
source_name: Fabrico - Air compressor troubleshooting

issue_description: Compressor loads and unloads or starts and stops every few seconds.
root_cause: Pressure band set too narrow, receiver too small for the demand pattern, or a leaking check valve.
recommended_fix: 1) Widen the pressure band as far as the process allows. 2) Check the check valve before blaming the controller. 3) Consider extra receiver volume.
source_name: Fabrico - Air compressor troubleshooting

issue_description: Air pressure at the machine is much lower than at the compressor outlet.
root_cause: Pressure drop from clogged filters, leaking joints, undersized or twisting pipework, or water and oil contamination in the lines.
recommended_fix: 1) Fit pressure gauges at several points to find where it drops. 2) Clean or replace clogged filters. 3) Fix leaking seals and connectors. 4) Replace undersized pipe with the right diameter and straighter layout.
source_name: Atlas Copco - Pressure drop in compressed air systems

issue_description: Compressor makes a knocking or rattling noise and vibrates on its base.
root_cause: Loose mounting bolts, worn bearings or connecting rod parts on a piston unit, or a failing coupling.
recommended_fix: 1) Stop the machine and lock out. 2) Tighten mounting and guard bolts. 3) Check the coupling and drive belt. 4) Have a technician inspect bearings if the noise continues.
safety_note: Rotating parts: lock out before removing guards.

issue_description: Safety valve on the air receiver keeps popping off.
root_cause: Pressure switch or unloader not cutting out at the set pressure, or a faulty pressure control.
recommended_fix: 1) Stop the compressor. 2) Check cut-out pressure against the gauge. 3) Replace a faulty pressure switch or unloader. 4) Never adjust or plug the safety valve.
safety_note: An over-pressurised receiver can burst: never tamper with the safety valve.

issue_description: Boiler has no heat or has shut itself down on a safety lockout.
root_cause: A dirty or faulty igniter, a dirty flame scanner, a weak ignition transformer, interrupted fuel supply, a low-water lockout, a failed burner motor, a bad gas valve or a flame safeguard control fault.
recommended_fix: 1) Make sure the manual fuel valves are open and gas or oil supply is normal. 2) Look at the sight glass for the right water level. 3) Check the flame scanner for dirt. 4) Call the boiler service company for fuel-train, wiring or control repairs.
safety_note: Never bypass a safety device or work on the fuel train or pressure vessel yourself.
source_name: Cole Industrial - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Steam boiler is running but plant steam pressure and output are too low.
root_cause: Load above capacity, a failing feedwater pump, deaerator trouble, steam leaks, steam traps stuck open, condensate return problems, or scale on the heating surfaces.
recommended_fix: 1) Check whether new equipment or simultaneous processes are overloading it. 2) Read the feedwater line pressures. 3) Look for steam leaks and failed traps. 4) Have scale cleaned off if suspected.
source_name: Cole Industrial - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Fuel bill for the boiler keeps climbing and the flame looks lazy or yellow.
root_cause: Poor air-to-fuel ratio, faulty modulation, sooty or fouled burner and tubes, scaled tubes, damaged insulation or steam leaks.
recommended_fix: 1) Have the burner tuned with a calibrated combustion analyser. 2) Check whether it short-cycles or sits on high fire. 3) Clean soot from the fireside. 4) Repair damaged insulation and steam leaks.
source_name: Cole Industrial - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Boiler does not follow demand; temperature or pressure controls seem wrong or erratic.
root_cause: Drifted setpoints, a failed pressure or temperature control, a sticking modulating motor, a dirty or failed flame sensor, or a communication fault.
recommended_fix: 1) Verify the setpoint calibration. 2) Watch whether the modulating motor reacts to load changes. 3) Clean the flame sensor. 4) If any safety or operating control is suspect, do not run the boiler.
safety_note: Do not operate the boiler if a safety device or primary operating control is suspected faulty.
source_name: Cole Industrial - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Steam is made but little reaches the process, with banging or water carried into the steam lines.
root_cause: Blocked or restricted piping, steam traps stuck open or shut, condensate backing up, or foaming and priming caused by high dissolved solids in the boiler water.
recommended_fix: 1) Walk the steam distribution system. 2) Check for condensate back-up and test the traps. 3) Review water treatment and blowdown.
source_name: Cole Industrial - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Water is leaking from the boiler shell, there is a smell of gas, or a loud banging comes from the boiler.
root_cause: Possible vessel failure, fuel leak or combustion problem: these are emergency conditions.
recommended_fix: 1) Carry out the emergency shutdown procedure at once. 2) Evacuate the area if gas is smelt. 3) Do not restart. 4) Call a qualified boiler contractor.
safety_note: Emergency: shut down immediately and do not attempt a restart.
source_name: Cole Industrial - Boiler troubleshooting

issue_description: Hot-water boiler makes kettling, rumbling or banging noises while heating.
root_cause: Limescale on the heat exchanger or poor circulation causing local steam bubbles.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch off and let it cool. 2) Check the system pressure and the pump. 3) Have the heat exchanger descaled or flushed by a service engineer.

issue_description: Pressure relief valve discharges water from the boiler or heating system.
root_cause: System pressure too high from a waterlogged expansion vessel or a leaking fill valve.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the pressure gauge. 2) Check the expansion vessel charge. 3) Close or replace a leaking filling loop. 4) Do not plug the relief valve.
safety_note: Discharged water can be scalding hot.

issue_description: Water level in the gauge glass drops and the boiler trips on a low-water alarm.
root_cause: Feedwater supply failure, a closed feed valve, or a drain or blowdown valve left open or leaking.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the feed pump and valves. 2) Check blowdown and drain valves are shut. 3) Never top up a hot, dry boiler: let it cool before refilling.
safety_note: Adding cold water to an overheated empty boiler can cause an explosion.

issue_description: Fridge runs but food is only lukewarm and not cold enough.
root_cause: Too little clearance around the cabinet, blocked internal vents, too little food stock, wrong temperature setting, a heat source nearby, hot food put in, dirty or worn door seals, or frequent door opening.
recommended_fix: 1) Give the cabinet the clearance the maker specifies. 2) Keep food away from the internal vents. 3) Lower the temperature setting. 4) Clean the door seals and test them with a paper strip. 5) Let hot food cool first.
source_name: Samsung Support - Cooling issues with refrigerator or freezer

issue_description: Refrigerator or freezer does not cool at all.
root_cause: No power, the unit left in a demo or shop mode that turns cooling off, dirty or failing door seals, or a sealed-system fault.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the power supply and display lights. 2) Look for a cooling-off or demo mode message and switch it off. 3) Check the door seals and alignment. 4) Unplug for two minutes and restart, then wait several hours. 5) Call service if it stays warm.
source_name: Samsung Support - Cooling issues with refrigerator or freezer

issue_description: Lettuce, milk and drinks freeze solid in the fridge compartment.
root_cause: A quick-cool feature left on, food pushed against the back wall or vents, vents iced over, or room temperature outside the unit's range.
recommended_fix: 1) Turn the quick-cool feature off. 2) Move food away from the vents. 3) Clear ice from blocked vents. 4) Keep the room within the temperature range the maker gives.
source_name: Samsung Support - Cooling issues with refrigerator or freezer

issue_description: Ice maker is not making ice or has stopped producing cubes.
root_cause: Fridge too warm, clogged water filter, ice stuck in the mould, or a blocked feeler arm or kinked water line.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the fridge and freezer temperatures. 2) Replace a clogged water filter. 3) Free ice stuck in the mould and check the feeler arm. 4) Check the supply line is open and not kinked.
source_name: GE Appliances - Refrigerator and freezer support

issue_description: Water dispenser is slow or gives hardly any water.
root_cause: A clogged or partly clogged water filter, or a new fridge whose reservoir is not yet full.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the water filter. 2) On a new unit allow time for the tank to fill. 3) Check the supply line for kinks.
source_name: GE Appliances - Refrigerator and freezer support

issue_description: Water is dripping or pooling around the fridge or ice maker.
root_cause: Loose water line fittings, a leaking water valve or fill tube, a blocked or overflowing defrost drain, or an unlevel cabinet.
recommended_fix: 1) Unplug the unit. 2) Tighten fittings and check the valve and fill tube. 3) Clear the defrost drain. 4) Level the cabinet.
safety_note: Unplug the fridge or ice maker before working on a water leak to reduce shock risk.
source_name: GE Appliances - Refrigerator and freezer support

issue_description: Thick frost builds up on the freezer back wall and the fridge does not cool well.
root_cause: Defrost heater, defrost sensor or timer failure, or a door seal letting humid air in.
recommended_fix: 1) Unplug and fully defrost. 2) Check the door seals. 3) If frost returns within weeks, have the defrost system tested and the faulty part replaced.

issue_description: Compressor clicks on and off or the fridge hums and never starts the cooling cycle.
root_cause: A failed start relay or overload device, or a compressor with a seized motor.
recommended_fix: 1) Unplug and wait five minutes, then restart. 2) If it still clicks and trips, have a technician test the start relay and compressor windings.
safety_note: Do not handle the sealed refrigerant system yourself.

issue_description: Commercial water chiller delivers water warmer than set point.
root_cause: Dirty condenser, low chilled-water flow, low refrigerant charge, or a faulty expansion valve.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the condenser coils or tubes. 2) Check chilled-water flow and strainers. 3) Have a certified technician check the refrigerant charge.
safety_note: Refrigerant work must be done by a certified technician.

issue_description: Refrigerator is very noisy, with a loud buzzing or rattling from the back.
root_cause: A condenser or evaporator fan hitting ice or debris, loose panels or pipes, or an unlevel cabinet.
recommended_fix: 1) Level the cabinet. 2) Pull it out and check the back for loose pipes or items. 3) Have the fans inspected if the noise continues.
safety_note: Unplug before removing any back panel.

issue_description: Axis alarm: an axis lags or draws excessive current and the CNC stops.
root_cause: A crash, mechanical binding, lubrication starvation, a failing motor or amplifier, chips packed on the ways, a dragging brake or a cut that is too heavy.
recommended_fix: 1) Jog the axis slowly through its full travel while watching the load meter. 2) Check way lubrication. 3) Compare the load on the other axes. 4) Clean the ways and covers.
safety_note: Lock out and tag out before opening the cabinet: servo drives keep a dangerous charge after power-off.
source_name: Fabrico - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Low air, lubrication or coolant alarm on the machine control.
root_cause: Empty tank, clogged line, failed pump, compressor or regulator trouble, leaks or an undersized air line.
recommended_fix: 1) Refill the tank. 2) Inspect lines and metering points. 3) Watch the gauge at the machine while it cycles.
source_name: Fabrico - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: High voltage or regen resistor overheat alarm on the CNC.
root_cause: High utility voltage, a wrong transformer tap, or heavy acceleration and deceleration duty.
recommended_fix: 1) Have an electrician measure the incoming supply. 2) Verify the transformer taps. 3) Reduce aggressive accel/decel moves if the duty is the cause.
safety_note: Electrical work must be done by a qualified electrician.
source_name: Fabrico - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Axis overtravel or soft-limit alarm during or after a program.
root_cause: A crash, a bad tool or work offset, or a lost reference position.
recommended_fix: 1) Jog the axis away from the limit. 2) Check the offsets in the program. 3) Re-home the machine. 4) Look for crash damage before running again.
source_name: Fabrico - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Servo or spindle motor thermal trip: motor overheated alarm.
root_cause: Sustained overload, mechanical binding or a high duty cycle.
recommended_fix: 1) Let the motor cool. 2) Find the mechanical reason for the load. 3) Reduce cutting load or duty cycle.
source_name: Fabrico - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Encoder fault alarm and the axis position is not trusted.
root_cause: A contaminated or failing encoder, or a damaged encoder cable or connector.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect the encoder cable and connector. 2) Look for coolant that has got into the encoder. 3) Replace the encoder or cable if damaged.
safety_note: Lock out power before opening the cabinet or touching connectors.
source_name: Fabrico - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Communication fault between the control and the motor control board, with random alarms.
root_cause: Electrical noise, grounding faults or a failed board.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the grounding and shielding. 2) Check the cable connections. 3) Have a technician test the board if the fault persists.
safety_note: Lock out before opening cabinets.
source_name: Fabrico - Haas CNC alarm codes troubleshooting

issue_description: Lathe leaves a rough chattering finish on the part and the spindle sounds harsh.
root_cause: Too long a tool overhang, a worn insert, wrong speed and feed, loose workholding or worn spindle bearings.
recommended_fix: 1) Shorten the tool overhang. 2) Replace the insert. 3) Change speed and feed away from the resonance. 4) Check chuck and tailstock hold. 5) Have spindle bearings checked if chatter remains.

issue_description: CNC spindle runs hot or throws an overheat alarm.
root_cause: Failed spindle cooling, a clogged filter, low lubricant or sustained heavy cutting.
recommended_fix: 1) Check spindle coolant or chiller flow. 2) Clean air filters. 3) Check lubricant levels. 4) Lower the cutting load.

issue_description: Parts come out of tolerance and dimensions drift during the day.
root_cause: Thermal growth of the machine, backlash or worn ball screws, worn tooling, or lost tool offsets.
recommended_fix: 1) Warm the machine up before cutting. 2) Check and update tool offsets. 3) Measure backlash and have worn ball screws or nuts replaced.

issue_description: Forks lift slowly or the load drifts down while raised.
root_cause: Contaminated or low hydraulic fluid, mast seal leaks or a failing lift cylinder.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the hydraulic fluid level and filters. 2) Inspect the mast seals and cylinders for leaks. 3) Do not postpone the repair.
safety_note: Do not operate a truck whose load can drift down.
source_name: Racklify - Counterbalance forklift maintenance checklist and safety practices

issue_description: Truck vibrates badly while driving.
root_cause: Damaged tyres, worn wheel bearings or, on engine trucks, worn engine mounts.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect tyres for damage and flats. 2) Check the wheel bearings. 3) On engine trucks verify the engine mounts.
source_name: Racklify - Counterbalance forklift maintenance checklist and safety practices

issue_description: Brakes feel weak or the pedal sinks.
root_cause: Worn pads, worn drums or discs, or degraded hydraulic brake fluid.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect the brake pads. 2) Adjust or replace drums or discs. 3) Check the condition of the brake fluid.
safety_note: A truck with poor brakes must be taken out of service.
source_name: Racklify - Counterbalance forklift maintenance checklist and safety practices

issue_description: Electric forklift battery will not hold a charge and runs flat quickly.
root_cause: Sulphated battery plates or poor charging practice.
recommended_fix: 1) Set up a battery routine of correct watering, equalising and full charge cycles. 2) Have the battery tested if it still will not hold a charge.
safety_note: Use lockout/tagout and proper PPE for battery work; battery acid and hydrogen are hazardous.
source_name: Racklify - Counterbalance forklift maintenance checklist and safety practices

issue_description: Forks rise unevenly or the mast shudders as it lifts.
root_cause: Mast binding, worn lift chains, or air in the hydraulic system.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect and lubricate the mast channels. 2) Check chain wear and tension. 3) Bleed air from the hydraulic system.

issue_description: Steering is loose or sloppy with a lot of play.
root_cause: Worn tie rods or a worn steering gear, or low power-steering fluid.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the steering fluid. 2) Measure the free play. 3) Replace worn tie rods or steering parts.
safety_note: Take the truck out of service if steering is unreliable.

issue_description: Electric forklift will not move or lift when the key is on.
root_cause: Flat battery, loose battery connector, an open emergency stop, a seat or interlock switch, or a blown fuse.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the battery charge and connector. 2) Reset the emergency stop. 3) Check seat switch and direction lever. 4) Check fuses.
safety_note: Disconnect the battery before working on electrical parts.

issue_description: Engine forklift cranks but will not start, or stalls under load.
root_cause: No or dirty fuel, a clogged filter, a weak battery, or ignition problems.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the fuel level and shut-off. 2) Replace clogged fuel and air filters. 3) Check battery and cables. 4) Have the ignition or injection checked.
safety_note: LPG trucks: check for leaks with the cylinder valve shut and stay clear of ignition sources.

issue_description: Hydraulic oil is dripping from the mast or the lift cylinder.
root_cause: Worn seals or damaged hoses and fittings.
recommended_fix: 1) Clean the area to locate the leak. 2) Tighten fittings. 3) Replace leaking hoses or seals. 4) Top up the fluid.
safety_note: Oil on the floor is a slip hazard: clean it up and tag the truck.

issue_description: Forklift engine overheats or the temperature gauge climbs.
root_cause: Low coolant, a blocked radiator or a failed fan or thermostat.
recommended_fix: 1) Stop and let it cool. 2) Check coolant level and radiator for debris. 3) Test the fan and thermostat.
safety_note: Do not open a hot radiator cap.

issue_description: UPS keeps beeping and a light is on: either four beeps every half minute with an amber on-battery light, or a long beep every few hours with a red replace-battery light.
root_cause: Four beeps with the amber light: mains power was lost and the UPS is running on its battery. A minute of beeping every few hours with the red replace-battery light: the battery failed its automatic self-test and is worn out.
recommended_fix: 1) On-battery alarm: check the building supply, the UPS plug and input breaker, restore mains power and shut equipment down gracefully if it does not return. 2) Replace-battery alarm: fit a new battery module of the correct type and run a self-test to clear it.
safety_note: Follow the maker's battery instructions: UPS batteries can deliver high current.
source_name: APC / Schneider Electric - Smart-UPS audible alarms (FAQ FA156554)

issue_description: UPS gives one loud continuous tone and the red overload light is on.
root_cause: The connected equipment draws more than the UPS capacity.
recommended_fix: 1) Unplug non-essential equipment from the UPS. 2) Keep removing load until the tone stops. 3) Move big loads such as printers to a plain surge outlet.
source_name: APC / Schneider Electric - Smart-UPS audible alarms (FAQ FA156554)

issue_description: UPS chirps every few seconds and the replace-battery light flashes.
root_cause: The internal battery connector is loose or the battery is not connected.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch the UPS off and unplug it. 2) Open the battery compartment and reseat the connector. 3) Restart and run a self-test.
safety_note: Unplug the UPS before touching the battery connector.
source_name: APC / Schneider Electric - Smart-UPS audible alarms (FAQ FA156554)

issue_description: UPS clicks or hums softly while the mains is present and the voltage seems to change.
root_cause: The automatic voltage regulation is boosting or trimming input voltage that is too low or too high: normal operation.
recommended_fix: 1) No repair needed. 2) If it happens constantly, have an electrician check the supply voltage at the outlet.
source_name: APC / Schneider Electric - Smart-UPS audible alarms (FAQ FA156554)

issue_description: UPS keeps beeping continuously just before it switches the computers off during a power cut.
root_cause: The battery is nearly flat after running on battery power, so shutdown is imminent.
recommended_fix: 1) Save your work and shut equipment down now. 2) Afterwards test runtime and replace an ageing battery.

issue_description: UPS will not switch on or has no output even though it is plugged in.
root_cause: A tripped input breaker, a deeply discharged or dead battery, or a failed inverter board.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the wall socket and the UPS breaker button. 2) Charge the UPS for several hours. 3) If it stays dead, have the battery and unit tested.

issue_description: Backup runtime is only a minute or two instead of the expected time.
root_cause: An old battery (typically a few years in service), an overloaded UPS, or a battery that was never fully charged.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the load against capacity. 2) Run a self-test and runtime calibration. 3) Replace the battery if capacity has fallen.

issue_description: UPS case is hot, the fan is loud, or the battery compartment is swollen.
root_cause: A blocked fan or vents, an overloaded unit or a swelling battery.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch off and unplug. 2) Clear dust and keep vents free. 3) Do not use a UPS with a swollen battery: replace the battery module.
safety_note: A swollen battery is a fire and chemical hazard: stop using the unit.

issue_description: Inverter or UPS trips off immediately when a large motor or laser printer starts.
root_cause: Inrush current from the load is higher than the UPS can supply.
recommended_fix: 1) Disconnect the motor or printer load. 2) Use a larger UPS or run those devices from non-UPS outlets.

issue_description: Laptop screen stays black or flickers although the power light is on.
root_cause: A fault in the LCD panel or graphics, brightness turned to minimum, or a bad display connection.
recommended_fix: 1) Press the brightness-up key several times. 2) Plug in an external monitor to see whether the laptop itself works. 3) Run the built-in LCD self-test. 4) Contact support if only the laptop screen is dead.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot power issues on a Dell laptop

issue_description: Laptop is completely dead: no lights, no fan, nothing happens when the power button is pressed.
root_cause: A system board fault, a dead CMOS battery, loose memory modules or a fully drained battery.
recommended_fix: 1) Run the system board self-test. 2) Do a real-time clock reset by holding the power button as the maker instructs. 3) Reseat the memory. 4) Replace the CMOS battery if the earlier steps fail.
safety_note: Guard against electrostatic discharge when opening the laptop.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot power issues on a Dell laptop

issue_description: Laptop shuts itself off from heat and will not start again for a while.
root_cause: Blocked air vents or a hot CPU, often from using the laptop on a bed or sofa.
recommended_fix: 1) Blow dust from the vents with compressed air. 2) Use the laptop on a hard flat surface. 3) Leave clearance around the vents.
safety_note: Do not blow the dust out with your mouth (moisture damages electronics) and avoid vacuum cleaners on the vents.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot power issues on a Dell laptop

issue_description: Laptop was dropped or had liquid spilled on it and will not power on.
root_cause: Internal damage or a deformed case.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch off and disconnect power. 2) Look for broken plastic, cracks or deformation. 3) Take it to a repair service; do not keep trying to power it on.
safety_note: Do not run a laptop with liquid inside it.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot power issues on a Dell laptop

issue_description: Computer stopped working right after new memory or a drive was installed.
root_cause: A faulty new part or an incorrect installation.
recommended_fix: 1) Remove and reinstall the part following the manual. 2) Try with the original part. 3) Contact the maker's support if it still fails.
safety_note: Guard against electrostatic discharge when handling parts.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot power issues on a Dell laptop

issue_description: Laptop keyboard or touchpad is lifting, the base rocks on a table and the case seam is uneven.
root_cause: A swollen lithium-ion battery from age, charge cycles or heat.
recommended_fix: 1) Stop using and charging it. 2) Have the swollen battery replaced before further use.
safety_note: A swollen battery can catch fire: do not press on it or puncture it.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot power issues on a Dell laptop

issue_description: Laptop will not power on after being carried or knocked.
root_cause: Memory modules have worked loose.
recommended_fix: 1) Power down and remove all power. 2) Reseat the memory modules following the manual.
safety_note: Guard against electrostatic discharge.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot power issues on a Dell laptop

issue_description: Laptop fan runs at full speed all the time and the machine is loud.
root_cause: Sustained high CPU load, obstructed vents or dust on the cooling fins.
recommended_fix: 1) Check Task Manager for the program using the CPU. 2) Disable unneeded startup programs. 3) Clean the vents. 4) Run the maker's fan diagnostic.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot overheating, shutdown or thermal issues

issue_description: The cooling fan does not spin at all and the computer gets hot.
root_cause: A fan hardware fault.
recommended_fix: 1) Run the fan diagnostic test from the BIOS or support tool. 2) If it fails, contact the maker for a replacement fan. 3) Do not keep using the computer under load.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot overheating, shutdown or thermal issues

issue_description: Laptop is hot and slow only when one particular program is open.
root_cause: A single application using excessive CPU.
recommended_fix: 1) Open Task Manager and find the heavy process. 2) Close or update that program. 3) Check for background updates or malware.
source_name: Dell Support - Troubleshoot overheating, shutdown or thermal issues

issue_description: Laptop is very slow, programs take ages to open and the disk light stays busy.
root_cause: Too many startup programs, a nearly full or failing disk, malware, or too little memory.
recommended_fix: 1) Remove startup programs. 2) Free disk space. 3) Run an antivirus scan. 4) Check disk health and upgrade to an SSD or more RAM if needed.

issue_description: Laptop battery shows plugged in but not charging.
root_cause: A faulty or frayed charger, a damaged charging port or a worn battery.
recommended_fix: 1) Try a known-good charger of the right rating. 2) Inspect the cable and port for damage. 3) Replace the battery if it is worn.
safety_note: Stop using a damaged charger or cable.

issue_description: Router lights are all off.
root_cause: The router is unplugged or not powered on.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the power cable and socket. 2) Make sure the adapter is plugged in and switched on.
source_name: eSafety Commissioner (Australia) - What to do when your home internet drops out

issue_description: Router has flashing or red lights and no internet.
root_cause: A problem with the internet connection.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch the router off at the power, wait, and switch it on again. 2) If the red light stays, check the provider's outage page or call support.
source_name: eSafety Commissioner (Australia) - What to do when your home internet drops out

issue_description: Phone or laptop shows connected to Wi-Fi but there is no internet.
root_cause: An outage outside the home or a Wi-Fi signal problem.
recommended_fix: 1) Disconnect and reconnect to the Wi-Fi. 2) Plug a computer in by cable to test. 3) Check the provider for an area outage.
source_name: eSafety Commissioner (Australia) - What to do when your home internet drops out

issue_description: Wi-Fi is weak in some rooms and the connection keeps dropping there.
root_cause: The router is too far from the devices.
recommended_fix: 1) Move the router closer to where it is used. 2) Add a Wi-Fi extender if needed.
source_name: eSafety Commissioner (Australia) - What to do when your home internet drops out

issue_description: Internet drops for everyone at the same time while the router seems fine.
root_cause: Maintenance or technical problems on the provider side.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the provider website or app for outage status. 2) Wait for restoration or report the fault.
source_name: eSafety Commissioner (Australia) - What to do when your home internet drops out

issue_description: Switch port has no link light and the device plugged in cannot reach the network.
root_cause: No cable, the wrong port, no power at the far device, a bad or wrong type of cable, a faulty patch panel or media converter, or a disabled or faulty port.
recommended_fix: 1) Test the cable with a known-good device. 2) Swap the cable and the port. 3) Reseat connectors and bypass the patch panel if possible. 4) Check the interface for shutdown or error-disabled status.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Network is extremely slow with many errors on one link, and collisions on a full-duplex port.
root_cause: A duplex mismatch: one end full-duplex and the other half-duplex, often from setting one side by hand.
recommended_fix: 1) Set both ends to auto-negotiate, or hard-set both identically. 2) Update the NIC driver if it is a third-party card. 3) Recheck counters afterwards.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Switch port shows err-disabled and stays down.
root_cause: EtherChannel misconfiguration, duplex mismatch, BPDU guard triggered, or a one-way link detected by UDLD.
recommended_fix: 1) Find the cause in the switch log. 2) Fix the cause. 3) Re-enable the port manually or configure errdisable recovery.
safety_note: If the cause is not fixed the port will err-disable again.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: CRC and frame errors keep counting up on a switch port.
root_cause: Noise or a bad cable, a faulty port or NIC, or a duplex mismatch.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the cable with a known-good one. 2) Check duplex settings on both ends. 3) Swap the port or NIC if errors continue.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Whole LAN becomes very slow or unreachable and all switch lights blink at once.
root_cause: A spanning-tree loop: a blocked port wrongly starts forwarding because it stopped receiving BPDUs, for example over a one-way link.
recommended_fix: 1) Find out why BPDUs stopped arriving. 2) Check for unidirectional links (UDLD helps). 3) Enable loop guard on non-designated ports.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Gigabit fibre or copper link will not come up.
root_cause: Mismatched transceiver types, wrong cable category or fibre type, wrong length, or crossed or reversed fibre pairs.
recommended_fix: 1) Use matching transceivers on both ends. 2) Use Cat 5e or better copper. 3) Check the fibre type and polarity. 4) Test the port with a known-good link.
safety_note: Ground new cable runs before connecting: static can damage switch ports.
source_name: Cisco - Troubleshoot switch port and interface problems

issue_description: Router keeps rebooting by itself or becomes very hot.
root_cause: A failing power adapter, overheating from blocked vents or a firmware bug.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the power adapter with the correct one. 2) Give the router airflow. 3) Update firmware.

issue_description: Camera picture is blurry or fuzzy, especially at night.
root_cause: A dirty lens, an extension cable that is too long, or a varifocal lens that is not focused.
recommended_fix: 1) Wipe the lens gently with a soft clean cloth. 2) Check the cable length is within limits. 3) Adjust focus and zoom on varifocal cameras.
safety_note: Do not use harsh or aerosol cleaners on the lens.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions

issue_description: Camera shows a black screen with no picture.
root_cause: A power or cable problem or a bad DVR/NVR input.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the camera power supply. 2) Try another port on the recorder. 3) Swap the cables.

issue_description: Camera image is green or pink.
root_cause: A glitch of the infrared cut filter or power or interference.
recommended_fix: 1) Move the camera slightly or toggle the IR lights. 2) Power the camera off and back on.

issue_description: Camera picture is washed out white during the day.
root_cause: The camera faces the sun, a spotlight or a glass window.
recommended_fix: 1) Reposition the camera away from direct light. 2) Fit a sunshade. 3) Adjust brightness and contrast.
safety_note: Do not point the camera straight at a glass window.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions

issue_description: Camera picture is too dark and details are lost.
root_cause: Too little light or exposure settings that are too low.
recommended_fix: 1) Adjust brightness and contrast. 2) Reposition the camera for better light. 3) Slide the sunshade back.

issue_description: Night vision is grainy and the picture is poor after dark.
root_cause: A poor night-vision design, no infrared cut filter or certain indoor lighting.
recommended_fix: 1) Use a camera with good night vision. 2) Consider colour night-vision models. 3) Remove strong reflective surfaces close to the camera.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions

issue_description: Bars or lines roll up the screen on the monitor.
root_cause: A ground loop or a faulty power supply.
recommended_fix: 1) Check and replace the camera power supply. 2) Check the grounding of the power adapters.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions

issue_description: Image flickers or the camera glitches and drops frames.
root_cause: Loose connections, unstable power, interference, or old firmware.
recommended_fix: 1) Check cables and connectors. 2) Restart the camera. 3) Install the latest firmware from the maker.
safety_note: Follow the firmware update instructions exactly.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions

issue_description: Vertical lines shake on the picture when the camera is connected to the recorder.
root_cause: The camera and recorder use different video standards (NTSC and PAL).
recommended_fix: 1) Use a camera and recorder with the same video standard. 2) Switch the standard in the recorder menu if available.
source_name: Reolink - Security camera picture problems and solutions

issue_description: IP camera keeps going offline or disconnecting from the network.
root_cause: Weak Wi-Fi, an IP address conflict, power interruptions or old firmware.
recommended_fix: 1) Move the camera nearer to the router or use a cable. 2) Give it a fixed IP address. 3) Check the power supply. 4) Update the firmware.

issue_description: RO purifier gives no water at all from the tap.
root_cause: Storage tank air pressure set wrong, the water supply is off, inlet pressure below about 40 psi, clogged pre-filters or membrane, a crimped line or a closed valve.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the supply is on and the feed valve is open. 2) Confirm inlet pressure is at least about 40 psi. 3) Set the empty tank pressure to the 5-7 psi range. 4) Replace clogged filters. 5) Straighten any kinked tubing.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Water comes out of the RO faucet very slowly and the tank takes ages to fill.
root_cause: Clogged pre- or post-filters, low tank air pressure, a fouled membrane or low incoming water pressure.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the filters. 2) Reset the tank air pressure to the 5-7 psi range when empty. 3) Allow several hours for the tank to refill. 4) Check inlet pressure.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Water drips from the RO membrane housing.
root_cause: The O-ring is not seated properly or the cap or body is cracked.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch off the water and relieve pressure. 2) Lubricate the O-ring with silicone grease and retighten the cap. 3) Replace cracked parts.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Water leaks from a filter housing of the purifier.
root_cause: A misplaced or dirty O-ring or a damaged housing.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the O-ring sits in its groove. 2) Clean and lubricate it. 3) Retighten the housing, or replace it if cracked.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: The RO drinking-water faucet drips or leaks at its base.
root_cause: A loose fitting, a faulty stem or a defective faucet.
recommended_fix: 1) Tighten the fittings and tubing. 2) Replace the faucet if it keeps leaking.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Purified water tastes or smells bad.
root_cause: A worn-out membrane, exhausted filters, a system that needs sanitising or water that has stood unused.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the filters. 2) Replace the membrane if its salt rejection has fallen too low. 3) Sanitise the system. 4) Drain the tank if it has not been used for several days.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: RO water looks cloudy or milky.
root_cause: A defective membrane, or just air in a newly installed system.
recommended_fix: 1) Let the system run for a few days; air-caused cloudiness clears. 2) Replace the membrane if the cloudiness stays.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: RO unit makes a gurgling or trickling noise at the drain.
root_cause: An air-gap faucet design, air in the lines or a drain line that does not run downhill.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the air-gap faucet is installed correctly. 2) Allow time for trapped air to clear. 3) Make sure the drain line slopes downhill.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: RO system never stops running and keeps sending water to drain.
root_cause: A faulty automatic shut-off valve, low tank or water pressure, a burst tank bladder or a worn flow restrictor.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the shut-off valve. 2) Raise the pressure toward 40 psi or more. 3) Check the tank air pressure. 4) Replace the tank or flow restrictor.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Water seeps from the tube connections and fittings of the purifier.
root_cause: A damaged fitting or tubing that was not pushed in fully.
recommended_fix: 1) Replace the damaged fitting. 2) Push the tubing fully into the fitting.
source_name: ESP Water Products - Reverse osmosis troubleshooting guide

issue_description: Purifier TDS reading is high and the water tastes salty although filters were replaced recently.
root_cause: A fouled or damaged membrane or a failed seal letting feed water bypass.
recommended_fix: 1) Measure TDS of feed and product water. 2) Replace the membrane. 3) Check the seals in the membrane housing.

issue_description: Washer will not fill with water and shows a water-supply error.
root_cause: A kinked, twisted or clogged inlet hose, or a loose hose connection.
recommended_fix: 1) Pull the washer out and look at the hoses at the back. 2) Straighten any kinks. 3) Check the hose is securely connected to the tap.
source_name: Asurion - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Washing machine will not drain and clothes stay in standing water.
root_cause: A clogged drain pump filter, a blocked drain hose or a failing drain pump motor.
recommended_fix: 1) Switch off and unplug. 2) Clean lint and debris from the drain pump filter. 3) Check the drain hose. 4) Run a spin-only cycle and listen for the pump; call a repairer if the motor is dead.
safety_note: Have towels ready: the drum water will pour out when the filter is opened. Unplug the washer first.
source_name: Asurion - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Washer will not spin or agitate and shows an error.
root_cause: An overloaded drum or a coin or other foreign object in the tub.
recommended_fix: 1) Remove some laundry. 2) Check the tub for coins and debris. 3) Spread the clothes evenly.
source_name: Asurion - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Washer stops mid-cycle with an unbalanced-load error.
root_cause: A very small load or clothes bunched on one side of the drum.
recommended_fix: 1) Pause the cycle. 2) Redistribute the laundry around the drum. 3) Restart.
source_name: Asurion - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Washing machine shakes, thumps and walks across the floor during spin.
root_cause: Machine legs not level or an uneven load.
recommended_fix: 1) Put a spirit level on top. 2) Adjust the feet until it is level and stable. 3) Spread clothes evenly.
source_name: Asurion - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Puddle of water appears under the washing machine.
root_cause: A cracked or torn hose, a damaged door gasket on a front loader, or a detergent drawer that is not closed or is clogged.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect the hoses and replace any that are damaged. 2) Check the door gasket for tears (replacement is a repair job). 3) Clean the detergent drawer and push it fully shut.
safety_note: Unplug the washer before looking behind it.
source_name: Asurion - Common LG washing machine problems

issue_description: Washer drum makes a loud rumbling or grinding noise when spinning.
root_cause: Worn drum bearings or worn suspension.
recommended_fix: 1) Check it is level and not overloaded. 2) Spin the empty drum by hand: a gritty rumble means worn bearings. 3) Have the bearings or suspension replaced.

issue_description: Door will not open at the end of the cycle.
root_cause: Water still in the drum or the door lock has not released.
recommended_fix: 1) Wait a few minutes. 2) Drain the machine. 3) If the lock stays stuck, switch off, wait, and use the emergency release.
safety_note: Do not force the door while there is water in the drum.

issue_description: Washing machine and clothes smell musty or mouldy.
root_cause: Mould and detergent residue in the drum seal and drawer from damp, closed-up conditions.
recommended_fix: 1) Wipe the door seal and drawer. 2) Run a hot maintenance wash with a washer cleaner. 3) Leave the door ajar after use.

issue_description: Too many suds and water overflowing from the washing machine.
root_cause: Too much detergent or the wrong detergent type.
recommended_fix: 1) Stop the cycle. 2) Run a rinse cycle. 3) Use the correct measured amount of low-suds detergent.

issue_description: Lift does not respond to the call buttons or stops working altogether.
root_cause: A power outage, a malfunctioning control system or a mechanical failure.
recommended_fix: 1) Check that power has been restored. 2) Read the control panel for error codes. 3) Call the lift maintenance company if it does not recover.
source_name: Infraspeak - 6 common lift issues and how to solve them

issue_description: Lift moves slowly or jerks and stutters between floors.
root_cause: Poor lubrication, worn parts, misaligned pulleys or a motor or drive problem.
recommended_fix: 1) Lubricate as the maker specifies. 2) Inspect and replace worn parts. 3) Realign pulleys. 4) Have the motor and drive repaired.
source_name: Infraspeak - 6 common lift issues and how to solve them

issue_description: Unusual noises or vibration while the lift travels.
root_cause: Loose or worn parts, misaligned components, damaged bearings or faulty controls.
recommended_fix: 1) Inspect brackets, bolts and screws and tighten or replace them. 2) Lubricate moving parts. 3) Have a technician inspect bearings and controls.
source_name: Infraspeak - 6 common lift issues and how to solve them

issue_description: Elevator doors do not close or open properly, or keep reopening.
root_cause: Misaligned door tracks, faulty sensors, worn rollers or a door operator problem.
recommended_fix: 1) Clear and realign the door tracks. 2) Clean the sensors. 3) Repair or replace worn rollers and faulty components. 4) Adjust the door operator.
source_name: Infraspeak - 6 common lift issues and how to solve them

issue_description: Lift stops at a level that does not match the floor and the step is uneven.
root_cause: Leveling sensor problems, misaligned guide rails, worn suspension ropes or uneven surfaces.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the sensors for alignment and cleanliness. 2) Examine and realign the guide rails. 3) Adjust or replace suspension ropes. 4) Have the controller recalibrated.
safety_note: A large gap or step at the door is a trip and fall hazard: restrict use until fixed.
source_name: Infraspeak - 6 common lift issues and how to solve them

issue_description: Oil is found in the lift pit or machine room of a hydraulic elevator.
root_cause: Damaged seals, faulty valves or a deteriorated hose.
recommended_fix: 1) Find the leak. 2) Repair or replace the seal, valve or hose. 3) Clean the area thoroughly. 4) Dispose of the oil properly.
source_name: Infraspeak - 6 common lift issues and how to solve them

issue_description: Passengers are stuck in the lift between floors.
root_cause: Power failure, a safety device that has tripped or a control fault.
recommended_fix: 1) Talk to the passengers through the alarm and tell them to stay calm. 2) Call the lift emergency service. 3) Do not try to open the doors or climb out.
safety_note: Only trained lift technicians or rescue services should release trapped passengers.

issue_description: Lift machine room is very hot and the lift trips out on motor overload.
root_cause: Poor ventilation in the machine room, a failed cooling fan or an overloaded motor.
recommended_fix: 1) Restore ventilation. 2) Check the cooling fan. 3) Have the motor and drive inspected.

issue_description: Lift cab buttons or floor indicators do not light or give wrong floor numbers.
root_cause: Loose wiring, failed button contacts or a faulty indicator board.
recommended_fix: 1) Report it to the lift maintenance company. 2) Do not open the panels yourself.
safety_note: Lift wiring carries live voltage: leave it to technicians.

issue_description: Solar inverter shows an error, repeated shutdowns, or produces zero output.
root_cause: An internal fault, abnormal grid conditions, excessive temperature, a DC input problem or a communication error.
recommended_fix: 1) Look at the inverter display and status light. 2) Write down the exact error code and model. 3) Look the code up in the manual and check the monitoring data. 4) Call the installer if the error returns.
safety_note: Never open the inverter, disconnect the DC cables or climb on the roof to investigate.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Inverter shows grid voltage, frequency or no-grid fault and stops generating.
root_cause: Grid voltage or frequency outside the permitted range, a grid outage, a loose AC connection or a tripped protection device.
recommended_fix: 1) Confirm the property has grid power. 2) Note the error. 3) Wait for automatic reconnection. 4) Have the installer inspect the AC wiring if it repeats.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Solar app says the system is offline or shows zero power although the sun is shining.
root_cause: A Wi-Fi outage, a replaced router or changed password, a disconnected communication dongle or a platform interruption.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the inverter's own display. 2) Reconnect the communication device as in the manual. 3) Confirm the router has internet.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Inverter is off or no AC output after a breaker tripped or an isolator was switched off.
root_cause: An electrical fault, overload, water ingress, a protection event or accidental shutdown during maintenance.
recommended_fix: 1) Check only clearly labelled, safely reachable breakers. 2) Follow the installer's instructions. 3) If the breaker trips again at once, leave it off and call the installer.
safety_note: Repeated resetting can hide a serious fault: leave a re-tripping breaker off.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Solar output drops at the same time each day or in one season.
root_cause: New or partial shading from trees, buildings, antennas, leaves, nests or snow.
recommended_fix: 1) Look for new obstructions. 2) Trim branches where possible. 3) Ask the installer about micro-inverters or optimisers for permanent shade.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Off-grid solar system does not charge the battery or shuts down early.
root_cause: Wrong voltage settings, loose DC wiring or the charge controller in protection mode.
recommended_fix: 1) Read the charge controller indicator lights. 2) Make sure the battery is not too deeply discharged. 3) Check the breaker between controller and battery is on.
safety_note: DC wiring can be dangerous: involve a qualified installer.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Panels produce less than usual and look dirty or damaged.
root_cause: Heavy dirt or bird droppings, shading, visible damage such as cracked glass, or an underperforming string.
recommended_fix: 1) Look from the ground at different times of day. 2) Clean only parts reachable from the ground. 3) Contact the installer for damage or a weak string.
safety_note: Do not touch damaged panels or cables: contact an installer.
source_name: SolaX Power - Solar system not working: troubleshooting

issue_description: Inverter reports an isolation or ground fault and stops.
root_cause: Insulation leakage from moisture, damaged DC cables or poor connections at the panels.
recommended_fix: 1) Do not reset repeatedly. 2) Have the installer measure insulation resistance and inspect DC cabling and connectors.
safety_note: A ground fault can cause electric shock or fire: do not touch the DC wiring.

issue_description: Inverter reduces output or shuts down on high temperature on hot days.
root_cause: Poor ventilation, a blocked heat sink or direct sun on the unit.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the space around the inverter is clear. 2) Clean dust from vents and filters. 3) Consider shading or relocating the unit.

issue_description: Inverter display is blank and the unit seems dead.
root_cause: No DC input from the panels, an off isolator or a failed power supply inside the inverter.
recommended_fix: 1) Check the DC and AC isolators. 2) Wait for daylight. 3) Call the installer if it stays blank in good sun.
safety_note: Do not open the inverter.
